question: A 65-year-old patient on mechanical ventilation develops ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). Tracheal aspirate Gram stain shows Gram-negative bacilli. Which empirical antibiotic regimen is most appropriate pending culture results?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Amoxicillin-clavulanate has poor anti-pseudomonal activity and inadequate penetration into lungs for VAP. It is not appropriate empirical coverage for suspected Pseudomonas VAP.

Correct. For VAP with suspected Pseudomonas aeruginosa, anti-pseudomonal beta-lactams (piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, meropenem, or imipenem) are the backbone. Combination with an aminoglycoside or ciprofloxacin is used in critically ill patients to provide synergy and broaden coverage pending sensitivity results.
Vancomycin covers MRSA but not Gram-negative pathogens; metronidazole covers anaerobes. This combination misses the suspected Pseudomonas entirely.

Oral bioavailability of ciprofloxacin is reasonable, but monotherapy with fluoroquinolones for Pseudomonas VAP is discouraged due to high resistance rates and the severity of VAP warranting IV combination therapy.

overallFeedback.feedback: For suspected Pseudomonas VAP, empirical therapy must include an anti-pseudomonal agent (pip-taz, cefepime, or carbapenem). Single agents with narrow spectrum (amoxicillin-clavulanate, vancomycin alone) will not cover this Gram-negative pathogen.
Well done. Pseudomonas VAP requires anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam coverage. De-escalate once sensitivities are back — double coverage is an empirical strategy, not definitive therapy.
